content.title: The Masters prize money: How much every player took home from Augusta National
content.text: Rory McIlroy will take home $4.5m after successfully defending the Green Jacket at Augusta to win his sixth major. That’s $300,000 more than the Northern Irishman banked when he completed the career Grand Slam last April. A brief history of the Masters prize money When the Masters was founded in 1934, Bobby Jones and Clifford Roberts were keen to attract as strong a field as possible. So they put up a $5,000 purse with $1,500 of that going to the winner – around $36,000 in today’s money. In contrast, the first prize at the US Open and PGA Championship in the same year was $1,000, while The Open champion took home just £100. (No, that’s not missing a zero.) Somewhat strangely, the purse fluctuated through the 1950s and ’60s, though the winner’s share always stayed the same or increased. Incidentally, the first player to head back down Magnolia Lane with a seven-figure paycheck was Tiger Woods – who else? – after his 2001 victory saw him put a second Green Jacket in his closet and just north of $1 million in his bank account. The sand isn’t sand, no ‘rough’, and other crazy Masters facts Why do Augusta caddies wear white jumpsuits? 2026 Masters prize money breakdown There is a record $22.5 million up for grabs to those teeing up at Augusta National, with $4.5m reserved for the champion – a number only matched by The Players Championship. Those who missed the cut will each take home $25,000 for their troubles. Amateur players, of course, are not eligible for prize money.
